method.label: Similarity, chord products, and the diagonal

annotationRationale: Similar-triangle ratios and chord products reduce the target to BD squared divided by 3. Supplementary cyclic angles and two cosine-law equations then determine that diagonal square.
sourceMethod: Followed the official similarity and power-of-a-point reduction, then the opposite-angle cosine-law calculation. Clarified the order B,Y,X,D and eliminated the cosine by adding the two equations with suitable multipliers.

review.mathCheck: Independently, XY=4d/9 and XD=d/4, so similarity gives XF/XC=16/9. Since X is inside the circle, XC·XG=XB·XD=3d²/16; hence XF·XG=d²/3. Supplementary opposite angles give (73−d²)/48=(d²−40)/24, yielding d²=51 and product 17, choice A. The order B,Y,X,D is correct; E and F lie on extensions opposite A and C, consistent with the official figure and the unsigned length ratios.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of numbered MAA solution 24 on pages 10–12. It preserves both similarities, the intersecting-chord product, and elimination between the two cosine-law equations. The expanded algebra is correct and reconstructible at AMC 12 level.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed nodes correctly identify similarity proportions, power of a point, and cosine-law elimination. AA similarity, cyclic supplementary angles, and the supplementary-cosine identity appropriately serve as background. No material omission or incorrect direct node.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The supplied exact links for cnm_271, cnm_272, cnm_255, and cnm_h064 fit AA similarity, corresponding-side proportions, supplementary cyclic angles, and cos(π−α)=−cos α. This demonstrates those steps, not every property within each topic. No CN link is supplied for power of a point or general cosine-law applications; none should be inferred.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: G-SRT.B.5 fits the similarity application. The partial links 8.G.A.5 and G-SRT.B.4 overlap through parallel-line angles and proportional sides, without establishing their theorems here. G-SRT.A.2/A.3 transformation definitions and AA derivation, and 8.EE.B.6 slope derivation, are not demonstrated. G-C.A.3 overlaps through cyclic angles, without constructions or proof. F-TF.A.3 overlaps through the supplementary-cosine identity, without unit-circle derivation or special-angle values; F-TF.A.4 parity/periodicity and G-SRT.C.7 complementary-angle aspects are unused. G-SRT.D.10/D.11 support cosine-law applications, without law proofs or sine-law coverage. These remain partial crosswalks. No US links are supplied for cnm_272 or power of a point.
